title: Why the Ancestral Puebloans left the Four Corners
summary: The main reason the Ancestral Puebloans moved away is unclear, though one consensus view combines pressure from newcomers with climate-driven crop failures.
why: Whole regions of homes were left behind within about two centuries.
question: Why did the Ancestral Puebloans leave their cliff and canyon homes in the 12th and 13th centuries?
evidence: Departures during the 12th and 13th centuries; proposed causes include drought, soil erosion, deforestation, hostile newcomers and religious change.
wouldSettle: Tree-ring dated records of drought, violence and migration compared across sites.

theories.name: Drought and climate
theories.idea: Prolonged drought and climate change caused crop failures.

theories.name: Numic newcomers
theories.idea: Pressure from Numic-speaking peoples moving onto the Colorado Plateau pushed them out.

theories.name: Religious or cultural change
theories.idea: Changing beliefs, perhaps with Mesoamerican influence, drew people elsewhere.
